items.title: A back button that takes you back
items.text: Open something from another module (a birthday from Home, a task from the calendar) and the top bar shows a back arrow. Tap it as many times as you like to retrace your steps. Open a module from the tab bar or More and you get the family bar instead.

items.title: Add and right-click on a computer
items.text: On a computer the top bar has + Add (or press N on any page). In the calendar, right-click a day to add an event, a to-do, a birthday or a trip on that date, or right-click an event to open, edit, recolour, duplicate or delete it.

items.title: Your own calendar categories
items.text: Add a category like Sports or Grandparents with its own icon and colour, and everyone in the family can pick it and filter by it. Events now get an icon guessed from their title (Parastas shows a church), and you can still tap the icon to change it.

items.title: The days inside an event
items.text: Events that last more than one day now list every day on their page. Mark days (like fish days in a fast) in one go with a weekend or Wed & Fri pattern, add a note or to-dos to a single day, and see them on that day in the calendar. Marks come back next year with a repeating event

items.title: Your AI assistant knows the days inside an event
items.text: A connected AI app can now see and change the marks and notes on each day of a long event, add to-dos to a single day, and list, add and rename your calendar categories. Ask it to mark the weekends of Lent as fish days, or to note the ferry time on day 2 of the trip.

fixes: On the calendar timeline, the "… left" note no longer covers the event under it: a row that leaves just folds away
A day mark or day note you delete now waits 30 days in Recently deleted, so you can bring it back

Calendar timeline: one-day things show their icon (a cake, a to-do circle, the event's own icon), rows that leave fold away with a short note saying what left, and a weekly event's label follows the week you're looking at

On the calendar timeline, birthdays, to-dos and one-day events stay for two weeks after you scroll past them and show up two weeks before they reach the screen, instead of popping in and out at the edges
Edits to shopping items and projects show the moment you close the sheet, without waiting for the save
Faster everywhere: the app opens about half a second sooner, Home, Contacts and Birthdays load several times faster, and tabs open instantly (refreshing quietly in the background)
Inside a module, + offers only what you can add there, starting with the tab you're on (Spending: an expense or a list)
The plan step says plainly that only you pay and everyone you add is free, and the total shows whether it's per year or per month
While you type during sign-up, the buttons at the bottom step out of the way so the field has room
An emailed invite only works for the person it was sent to, so opening it while signed in as someone else asks you to switch accounts first

items.title: Days to remember
items.text: A wedding, moving in, the day someone passed away: every yearly date now has a home. Celebrate days get a warm card on Home, quiet ones a calm one, and you choose if and when you get a reminder.

fixes: Save stays on top at the bottom of a sheet, instead of disappearing under the fields when the keyboard is open
The Add sheet opens on Classic and puts what this page adds first, like Add an item to buy in a shopping list

items.title: Hear about birthdays in time
items.text: Pick how many days ahead you want a reminder: one default for the family, or different for anyone. The reminder says the day and how old they turn.

items.title: Find the person first
items.text: Adding a birthday now searches your contacts, so nobody gets added twice. Tap anyone on the list to change their date or reminder.

items.title: Trips, faith, family, school, work
items.text: Give an event a category and filter the calendar with one tap: the chips sit above Agenda, Month and Timeline.

items.title: Say your list, see it land
items.text: Tap the mic and Shopping starts listening right away: your words appear as you speak, items pop in as you go, and a short pause wraps it up.

fixes: Shopping's Lists tab ends with Add a list, like Add a shop on Shops
Dictation says why it stopped, Done with nothing heard opens typing, and the phone's top bar turns dark with it
Dictation on iPhone works from the Home Screen app too
Calendar filters show on every view, so a filter can't quietly hide everything

items.title: A friendlier way in
items.text: Signing up and logging in got a fresh look: six boxes for your code, the email you used last time already filled in, a shortcut to your inbox, and a language picker.

items.title: Homer turns with your phone
items.text: Tilt your phone and Homer turns to follow. On an iPhone, tap him once to let him feel the motion.

items.title: A calmer sidebar
items.text: On a computer the sidebar now starts with your family, keeps your pinned modules up top, and puts Members and Settings at the bottom.

fixes: The Timeline settles on whole days, and today's line no longer cuts through the dates
Tapping an event's date opens a month calendar, and its times open the phone's picker
The Timeline shows birthdays, appointments and open to-dos too, each on its own row

items.title: 5 days free, no card
items.text: Every new family gets 5 days to try everything. Pick a plan when you're ready: one price covers the whole family, and Settings › Billing shows how many days are left.

items.title: A cleaner shopping list
items.text: One card per aisle, bought items sink to the bottom, and Hide bought keeps only what's left to grab. Tick something by mistake? Undo is right there. Filter by shop when a list spans a few.

items.title: Each list its own settings
items.text: The ⋯ on a list opens its settings: who can see it, default shop, sort, and how soon bought items clear away. Or clear them now.

fixes: Settings › Billing opens the plan page, with a way back while your free days last

items.title: Shops get their logo
items.text: Type Kaufland, mega or Lidl Romania and the shop shows its own logo. Local shops get their first letter.

items.title: Shopping settings, your way
items.text: Pick a default shop, turn off duplicate warnings, and let bought items clear themselves after a week. Drag your shops into the order you visit them.

items.title: Aisles that fit each shop
items.text: A new shop asks how it's laid out (grocery, DIY, pharmacy) and suggests one. Drag aisles into your walking order and see how many items each holds.

fixes: Another family's shop page can no longer be opened by its address
Refresh shows it's updating straight away

items.title: Pick a date from a calendar
items.text: Tap a task's date and a month calendar opens right in the sheet. Clear date is one tap.

items.title: New versions wait for you
items.text: When an update is ready, a small pill offers Refresh. It never reloads on its own or while you're typing.

items.title: Every day on screen, listed
items.text: Under the Timeline you now see what's in the days on screen, not just the one you tapped.

fixes: Names on the Timeline stay put while you swipe
A new list's name is ready to type over

items.title: Trips and holidays, one row each
items.text: The new Timeline shows the big stuff side by side and swipes freely, with Agenda and Month a tap away.

items.title: Move a task to any list
items.text: Pick a list, or make a new one with its own icon and colour, without leaving the task.

items.title: Tasks, redesigned
items.text: Lists with sub-tasks, who's on it at a glance, and Today, Tomorrow or a date in one tap.

items.title: Get the app
items.text: Using FamilyWell in a browser? Add it to your Home Screen for reminders on your phone.
